newsitem.title: PANAMA: Clinton unlikely to attend Panama Canal congress.
newsitem.headline: Clinton unlikely to attend Panama Canal congress.

text.p: President Bill Clinton is unlikely to attend an international conference on the future of the Panama Canal in Panama City in September, elminating a possible meeting with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui.
"The president was invited but in his reply it was unlikely that he would attend," Stacy White, a spokeswoman with the U.S. embassy in Panama, said on Tuesday.
"We do support the congress and we will send a high-level delegation," she said. "I can't speculate why he (the president) would not attend."
The Clinton announcement coincides with Lee's decision to go ahead with his visit to Panama for the Sept 7-10 conference.

Taiwan, considered a renegade province by Communist China, has contributed $800,000 to help organise the conference, which coincides with the 20th anniversary of the U.S.-Panamanian treaty under which the canal is to come under full Panamanian control in 1999.
The conference would have afforded Lee a rare chance to meet with Clinton and other world leaders.
But newspaper reports said U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and heads of several U.S. organisations would boycott the conference if Lee attended.
The reports said China had tried to use the United Nations to apply pressure on Panama -- one of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies -- to withdraw the invitation to Lee.
Former Panama Canal Commission director and the event's organiser Fernando Manfredo said: "We would greatly regret the absence of the United Nations secretary-general and hope it does not happen."

Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo Ponce de Leon, Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori and the Secretary General of the Organisation of American States, Cesar Gaviria, confirmed their attendance, according to communique released by Panama's Foreign Ministry.
